name: EBITDA_L3_growth_return_neighbors
mechanism: Within an industry, EV/EBITDA is roughly a function of expected growth and the return earned on reinvestment (value driver formula: multiple rises with growth when ROIC exceeds the cost of capital). Selecting same-industry peers that are closest in recent growth and ROIC should match the fundamentals that the industry median averages away.
prediction: Median |ln error| below the 0.333 industry-median baseline in at least 3 of 4 exploration years, with pooled median around 0.31.
compact: EV/EBITDA | screen same industry_l3 | rank sales_growth_1y 1, roic 1, log_sales 0.5 | k=8, median, min_peers=5 | fallback [same industry_l2] -> []
critic_reason: Value-driver logic (EV/EBITDA rises with growth when ROIC exceeds the cost of capital) is specific and sensible, the L3 screen plus growth/ROIC ranking implements it directly, nothing comparable has been tried, and the year-by-year prediction is falsifiable.

name: EBITDA_L2_risk_growth_harmonic
mechanism: EV/EBITDA reflects growth, profitability of growth and risk; leverage (net debt/EBITDA) and size proxy for risk and cost of capital. Using a broader 2-digit pool gives more candidates so the distance ranking can find close fundamental matches, and the harmonic mean limits the upward bias from high-multiple outliers.
prediction: Beats the industry median (0.333) and the Bhojraj-Lee warranted multiple (0.357) on pooled median error, and has a lower mean error than 0.513.
compact: EV/EBITDA | screen same industry_l2 | rank sales_growth_1y 1, roic 1, ebitda_margin 0.5, net_debt_to_ebitda 0.5, log_sales 0.5 | k=10, harmonic_mean, min_peers=5 | fallback []
critic_reason: Adding a risk dimension (net debt/EBITDA, size) on a broader L2 pool, aggregated with the harmonic mean, is a distinct economic idea from pure growth/return matching, and its numeric targets are falsifiable; the ebitda_margin feature is only loosely tied to the stated mechanism, so the proposer should justify it or drop it in later rounds.

name: EBITDA_L4_size_peers
mechanism: Firms in the same narrow 4-digit SIC line share product markets, cyclicality and technology, and close size matches share scale-related risk and liquidity premia. This is a refined version of the traditional analyst comp set, falling back to coarser industries only when the narrow set is too thin.
prediction: Pooled median error within 0.02 of the industry-median baseline or better, beating it in at least 2 of 4 years.
compact: EV/EBITDA | screen same industry_l4 | rank log_sales 1, sales_growth_1y 0.5 | k=6, median, min_peers=4 | fallback [same industry_l3] -> [same industry_l2]
critic_reason: Narrow 4-digit product-market peers matched on size are the classic analyst comp set with a clear risk and cyclicality rationale and a sensible fallback to coarser industries; the prediction is weak (it allows being up to 0.02 worse) but it is still falsifiable.

name: Sales_L2_margin_matched
mechanism: EV/Sales equals EV/EBITDA times EBITDA margin, so differences in margin dominate cross-sectional EV/Sales dispersion. Matching peers on EBITDA and gross margin within the same broad industry, plus growth, should remove most of the margin-driven error that plagues industry-median EV/Sales.
prediction: Pooled median error well below the 0.603 industry-median baseline (target under 0.50), beating it in all 4 exploration years.
compact: EV/Sales | screen same industry_l2 | rank ebitda_margin 2, gross_margin 1, sales_growth_1y 1 | k=8, median, min_peers=5 | fallback []
critic_reason: Because EV/Sales = EV/EBITDA x EBITDA margin, matching peers on margin is the first-order fix for EV/Sales dispersion; the heavy ebitda_margin weight within L2 implements this exactly and the 'all 4 years, under 0.50' prediction is sharply falsifiable.

name: Sales_crossindustry_fundamental_twins
mechanism: Valuation per dollar of sales is determined by how much of that sale becomes cash flow (margin), how fast it grows and capital needs (asset turnover); these economics can be matched across industry boundaries. Dropping the industry screen enlarges the pool so very close margin-growth twins can be found, with the harmonic mean controlling outlier peers.
prediction: Beats the industry median EV/Sales (0.603) and the Bhojraj-Lee warranted multiple (0.674) on pooled median error in at least 3 of 4 years.

name: SALES_crossindustry_profitability_harmonic
mechanism: A dollar of sales is worth what it turns into as cash flow: profitability (EBITDA and gross margin), growth and capital needs (asset turnover). Matching on these across all industries and taking the harmonic mean of the 20 nearest peers' sales multiples gives a stable, less skewed estimate that leans on economics more than SIC codes.

name: SALES_L3_margin_growth_nearest
mechanism: Inside a narrow 3-digit industry the business model is broadly shared, so what is left of the variation in sales multiples comes mostly from profitability and growth.
